json.title: [Feature]: Ability to use RLS with continuous aggregates, when the RLS rule matches the space partitioning key
json.body:
### What problem does the new feature solve?

**What problem does this feature solve**

One of the most popular (and most-suggested) ways of properly preventing data leakage in a multi-tenant SaaS architecture is to use row-level security (RLS). It's what my company does, and it's the only thing preventing us from adopting Timescale.

RLS already works with hypertables, but not with continuous aggregates. This prevents me from shipping awesome time-series dashboards to my users: my noisiest tables are full of samples from many customers, and need cached / materialized views to be performant.

**Alternatives Explored**

Alternative solutions are schema-per-tenant, database-per-tenant, or software-enforced isolation (or, I guess, don't use continuous aggregates - for us, the most valuable part of Timescale). 

I won't explain why schema-per-tenant or database-per-tenant are heavier lift solutions; that topic is well trodden. They are the right choice for some cases, but not mine, and not for many others.

Software-enforced isolation is good enough for low-risk use cases, but constant code churn and frequent releases makes it possible for a software bug to slip in that could be potentially damaging to users' privacy, and therefore damaging to our company's ability to keep our users safe.

We made the decision that RLS is the right trade-off between convenience and security. It adds a layer of protection if a software bug might otherwise leak data, and it limits the blast radius from a hack.

### What does the feature do?

**What this feature would do**

This feature would make it possible to enable certain (see below) RLS policies on hypertables that are used in continuous aggregates.

### Implementation challenges

**Implementation challenges**

Since continuous aggregates need to maintain partial aggregate values in the materialization hypertable, it presents a challenge with RLS: The RLS policy can be arbitrarily complex, and would need to be applied at the level of the partial aggregate in order to carry through to the final, aggregated query results.

**Possible implementations**

1. Option 1 posits that it could be possible to enforce RLS policies on just the continuous aggregate view (NOT the source table). In this world, the user (me) is responsible for ensuring that the needed columns are on the materialization table. This would be super easy to implement as a user. I could add "tenant_id" to my "group by" clause. In my materialized view, there'd be separate aggregates for all my tenants. A simple RLS policy on the materialized view would ensure I don't accidentally show one tenant's data to another.
2. Option 2 is tricky. Since Timescale already supports distributed hypertables with continuous aggregates, it should be possible to enforce RLS policies that only rely on columns **that are used in the hypertable space partitioning**. In other words, if I have a distributed hypertable that is chunked on 2 columns, "create_date" and "tenant_id", **theoretically** I should be able to enforce RLS on "tenant_id". Presumably, the materialization hypertable includes the space partitioning key (at least, that's how I imagine it would work - I could be way off base here). And if the materialization hypertable has the data partitioned by tenant_id already, then I should be able to enforce RLS all the way through the pipeline.

I'm making a lot of assumptions about how Timescale works from the outside, but it seems to me that if space-partitioned distributed hypertables can support continuous aggregates, then RLS policies that only affect those same columns should be possible to get working as well.

I'd love feedback on either of these items. I still continue to champion Timescale in my company, but this feature is currently a deal-breaker for us.

Thanks for the awesome product and I hope to hear from you soon!

Wait... I re-read [the docs](https://docs.timescale.com/use-timescale/latest/continuous-aggregates/create-a-continuous-aggregate/#query-continuous-aggregates) and they state "...make sure that the hypertable you are querying does not have row-level-security policies enabled."

Does this mean that applying RLS to the materialized view of the continuous aggregate is allowed? Is my "Option 1" implementation idea actually already allowed today?
Hello Rick, were you able to achieve some progress on this topic? We can enable RLS on continuous aggregates however not on hypertables with compression.
Unfortunately, I abandoned Timescale for my project. Hopefully you can get some help from the Timescale team!
